solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To loosen restrictions on ale? Risible, daft!

indicators.note: daft means silly or crazy, so these letters are to be jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker scoffs at a ridiculous proposal to relax the rules about beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daft' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of ALE and RISIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberalise a law or regime is to relax its rules and controls; the infinitive matches 'To loosen'.

clue.text: Woman of 51 with oomph

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
SA is short for sex appeal, which is oomph

explanation.surface: A woman of fifty-one still full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: SA (sex appeal) is a crossword staple for oomph or it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa is a woman's given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Lawyer creates obstacle restricting good person

indicators.note: restricting says the obstacle word hems in the next piece

parts.note: a barrier is an obstacle
ST, short for saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A lawyer puts hurdles in the way of a decent individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a lawyer who argues cases in the higher courts in Britain.

clue.text: Mature President taken in by nothing overseas

indicators.note: taken in by says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: rien is French for nothing, a foreign word from across the Channel

explanation.surface: An elderly head of state duped by a foreign scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overseas' signals a foreign word: the French RIEN, with P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature and to ripen both mean to develop fully with time.

clue.text: Authorise silence for recollection

indicators.note: re-collection, gathering the letters again in a new order, signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order permitting a minute's quiet for remembrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' is read as re-collection: the letters of SILENCE are collected again.
explanation.definitionFit: To license something is to grant official permission for it, to authorise it.

clue.text: Writer brought aboard ship meeting Her Majesty, a poet

indicators.note: brought aboard says a piece is placed inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a pen is a writing instrument, a writer
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An author boards a vessel to meet the Queen, along with a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene in praise of Elizabeth I, which suits the surface's meeting with Her Majesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Charity some volunteers may hold back

indicators.note: back says the held run of letters is read in the opposite direction
the words 'some volunteers' contain a run of letters across the word break, as if holding it

explanation.surface: A remark that some charity helpers might keep their goodwill in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may hold' picks out EVOL from somE VOLunteers, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible's older translations charity means love, as in 'faith, hope and charity'.

clue.text: Tree is more comfortable, less cold

indicators.note: less says the next letter is removed

parts.note: cosier means more comfortable
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A remark that a tree is a snugger and warmer spot.
explanation.walkthrough: COSIER without C.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose pliable twigs are used for basket-making.

clue.text: Petitions and submissions put away inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

parts.note: entries are things submitted, as to a competition
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Requests and forms are filed away in a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' is the idiom for eating food greedily, not storing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Entreaties are earnest requests or pleas, the same as petitions.

clue.text: Before journey start with safety belt

indicators.note: Before places the opening letter ahead of the next piece
start with points to the opening letter of the word safety

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Advice to buckle up before setting off on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safety belt' looks like one item; 'belt' is the definition, in the sense of a long narrow band such as a green belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt of land or colour is a long narrow band, the same thing as a strip.

clue.text: European composer uttered 'things to do'?

indicators.note: uttered means spoken, so the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Liszt was a Hungarian composer; a Czech is a European, so the phrase is heard as Czech Liszt

explanation.surface: Someone names a European composer and adds a note about tasks.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Liszt was Hungarian; the setter uses 'European composer' for the sounds CZECH + LISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: A checklist is a list of tasks to tick off, literally a set of things to do.

clue.text: Relations who couldn't help Humpty? No good!

indicators.note: No says the next letter is removed

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme all the king's horses and all the king's men could not put Humpty Dumpty together again

explanation.surface: Family members who could not mend Humpty Dumpty were useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' looks like a verdict on the helpers; it means remove G from KINGSMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinsmen are relatives by blood, the same as relations.

clue.text: Bit of a game in pub — sing out

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of sing are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub bursts into song during part of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SING to INGS. An innings is a team's or batter's turn at bat in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an innings is one side's turn at batting, a portion of the whole game.

clue.text: Bottle yet to be returned sitting round end of larder

indicators.note: sitting round says the backwards word encloses the next piece
to be returned says the word for yet is read backwards

parts.note: even and yet both mean still, as in even better or yet better

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of larder

explanation.surface: A bottle waiting to be taken back sits beside the end of the larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' turns EVEN into NEVE, which goes 'sitting round' R, the last letter of larder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, as in losing one's bottle.

clue.text: Man's heart's fluttering? That's no excuse for this!

definitions.text: Man's heart's fluttering? That's no excuse for this!

indicators.note: something fluttering moves erratically, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its letter s
taken with its letter s

explanation.surface: A man's infatuation does not justify pestering someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of MAN'S HEART'S, including both S's, rearrange; the whole clue also describes unwanted attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment is persistent unwanted attention or pressure, which a crush does not excuse.

clue.text: Maybe the piece doesn't require piano

indicators.note: doesn't require says the following letter is dropped

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A music critic says a composition works fine without the piano part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe the piece' reads as one phrase; 'Maybe the' is the definition by example, 'piece' the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the definite article, so it is an example of the word, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Could this be a little fellow's string of beads?

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
-let is a suffix meaning little, as in piglet

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a necklace might belong to a small man.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'little fellow' as CHAP with the diminutive ending -LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a short string of prayer beads, a third of a rosary.

clue.text: Violent male animal to huff and puff

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to breathe hard, to huff and puff

explanation.surface: An angry male beast snorting heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means unrestrained and fierce, so it can mean violent or wild.

clue.text: Woman beginning to prepare meal is willing to fit in

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of prepare

parts.note: a table can mean the food served, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A woman starting to cook a meal is happy to be accommodating.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptable person adjusts readily to new circumstances, willing to fit in.

clue.text: Way for sending out message sounding like 'Next monarch a king'

indicators.note: sounding like says the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: the next monarch is the heir and a king is male, so the phrase is heard as heir male

explanation.surface: A royal proclamation announcing that the next sovereign will be a king.
explanation.walkthrough: HEIR sounds like AIR and MALE like MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is a postal service carrying letters by plane, one method of dispatching a message.

clue.text: French mathematician gets the position in the Sorbonne

definitions.meaning: Pierre-Simon ... was a French mathematician and astronomer
the Sorbonne is a Paris university, so the phrase is put into French

explanation.surface: A French mathematician gets a post at the Paris university.
explanation.definitionFit: Laplace was a celebrated French mathematician, and la place is French for the position.

clue.text: What establishes authority and must be accepted by comrade

indicators.note: accepted by says the word and is taken into the word for comrade

parts.note: a mate is a friend or comrade

explanation.surface: A political slogan about a comrade having to accept authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandate is an official authorisation, the thing that gives someone authority to act.

clue.text: Arboreal mammals — planet is home to five pairs

indicators.note: is home to says the planet houses the next piece

parts.note: Mars is a planet
five pairs make ten

explanation.surface: Tree-dwelling animals live in couples on another world.
explanation.definitionFit: Martens are weasel-like mammals that live largely in trees.

clue.text: What has coils going round?

indicators.note: going round says the word for coils is turned back to front

parts.note: loops are coils

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what has windings running round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' reverses LOOPS. The whole clue also describes a spool of thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a reel around which thread, film or wire is wound in coils.

clue.text: Fastener at the bottom of yellow plant

indicators.note: in a down clue at the bottom of places the fastener below the other piece

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
a pin is a fastener

explanation.surface: A clip lying at the base of a yellow flower.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldry's gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpine, also spelt orpin, is a succulent plant of the stonecrop family.

clue.text: Model is tense

definitions.meaning: a model pupil or specimen is ideal, without flaw
in grammar this tense expresses completed action, as in 'I have eaten'

explanation.surface: A remark that a fashion model is nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect means flawless like a model example, and is also the name of a grammatical tense.

clue.text: Revoked legislation to be precise?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer in force
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A query whether a repealed law should be taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and precise both mean accurate in every detail.

clue.text: Lady and I facing endless danger

indicators.note: facing puts the I directly in front of the next piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a risk is a danger

explanation.surface: A woman and the speaker confront peril without end.
explanation.walkthrough: RISK loses its end to give RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's name, so it is an example of a lady.

clue.text: Discourse from displaced person right away

indicators.note: away says the following letter is taken out

parts.note: an expatriate lives away from their native country

explanation.surface: A refugee gives a lecture after being sent off immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately'; here it means drop R.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length on a subject, to discourse on it.

clue.text: A person in the club ignoring me? A warning sign

indicators.note: ignoring says the letters of me are left out

parts.note: a member belongs to a club
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club member who snubs the speaker gets a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the amber traffic light warns that the signal is about to change to red.
explanation.definitionFit: An amber light on traffic signals warns drivers to prepare to stop.

clue.text: Wine in marquee?

definitions.meaning: a dark red Spanish wine used in communion
a marquee is a large canvas shelter

explanation.surface: Drinks being served in a big canvas shelter at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent is an old name for a deep red Spanish wine, and a marquee is a large tent.

clue.text: Black dogs for fashionable types always on the move?

definitions.text: fashionable types always on the move

parts.note: jet black is deep black
setters are breeds of gun dog

explanation.surface: Dark-coated dogs that never stay put, like stylish travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsetters are wealthy fashionable people who travel constantly between glamorous places.
